name: Commodity Marketing & Trading

objectives.text: Identify examples of agricultural commodities bought and sold at market, such as corn, soybeans, wheat, cattle, and hogs
Describe places where farmers sell commodities, such as grain elevators, livestock auction barns, and processing plants
Describe how a commodity market allows farmers and buyers to trade agricultural products
Explain why farmers face price risk when commodity prices change between planting or breeding and the time of sale
Explain how grading standards such as No. 2 yellow corn or USDA quality grades make commodities interchangeable and affect the price paid
Interpret commodity price quotations using market units such as cents per bushel and dollars per hundredweight
Explain the difference between the cash market and the futures market for agricultural commodities
Explain the roles of commodity exchanges, hedgers, and speculators in agricultural futures trading
Locate and interpret commodity market data from sources such as USDA market news reports and futures exchange quotes
Calculate local basis and explain how basis connects the futures price to the cash price a producer receives
Compare cash contract types such as spot sales, forward contracts, basis contracts, and hedge-to-arrive contracts
Compare livestock marketing methods such as auction sales, direct sales to packers, and grid or formula pricing for an SAE or farm enterprise
Analyze how a short or long futures hedge protects a producer or buyer against adverse price movement
Calculate the net price from a completed futures hedge, including basis change, margin calls, and commission costs
Explain how buying put options sets a price floor and how call options set a price ceiling while keeping upside opportunity
Analyze seasonal price patterns and price charts to forecast likely price trends for a specific commodity
Analyze whether storing grain after harvest is profitable by comparing futures carry and expected basis improvement with storage costs
Evaluate marketing strategies such as cash sales, forward contracting, hedging, and options for selling a farm commodity
Develop a commodity marketing plan with price targets and timelines that uses cash sales, futures, and options to manage price risk
Evaluate the results of a completed commodity marketing plan against the season's price movement to judge its effectiveness

changes: Kept all six original objectives, lightly reworded, as they name real competencies. Added foundational objectives on selling points, price risk, grading standards, and reading price quotes for grades 5 to 7. Added grade 9 to 12 competencies on exchange roles, market data, basis, cash contract types, livestock marketing methods, hedge calculations, options, seasonal price analysis, storage decisions, and evaluating plan outcomes. Supply and demand theory, trade policy, and whole-farm business planning are left to the sibling sub-topics. Standards are attached only from grade 9 up and only where the objective teaches them.
